title: Reddit Stock Plunges 30% as Google's AI Search Hits Traffic and User Growth

Reddit Stock Plunges 30% as Google's AI Search Hits Traffic and User Growth

Trading disclosure

Reddit shares plunged 30.44% to $90.15 on Friday after CEO Steve Huffman warned that Google's AI-powered search features are cutting referral traffic and could shrink the platform's user base.

The selloff came after the company reported strong third-quarter results but issued a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast for the current quarter.

Myriad: Where does ETH go next? Click to make your prediction.

Reddit built much of its business around people discovering its discussions through Google searches, and those visitors are increasingly finding answers without ever clicking through to the platform. That puts pressure on the advertising business that has helped turn Reddit into one of the internet's fastest-growing publicly traded companies.

Reddit's third-quarter numbers initially looked healthy. Revenue climbed 53% year over year to $895 million, advertising revenue increased 54% to $847 million, and net income reached $283 million. Diluted earnings per share, which measure company profit attributable to each share while accounting for potential dilution, came in at $1.40, up 75% from a year earlier and above the $1.33 analyst consensus.

But the audience figures were less encouraging since Reddit reported 130.3 million daily active unique visitors, up 12% year over year but below the roughly 134 million analysts expected. In the U.S., the number actually fell 2% to 50.7 million, giving investors another reason to question whether the platform can maintain its growth.

Huffman delivered the warning during Thursday's earnings call, explaining that Google search referrals had fallen by more than one million on average every week during October, with the decline accelerating toward the end of the third quarter. If that pace continues, Reddit's total daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 from the current base of around 130 million.

Huffman pointed directly at Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, features that generate answers and summaries directly inside search results. Rather than sending users to websites to find information, Google increasingly gives them what they are looking for on its own page, pushing traditional search links further down.

Asked whether the changes were responsible for Reddit's declining search traffic, Huffman said the AI features had expanded aggressively in the U.S. and internationally. "The AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know," he told investors.

That creates an awkward situation for Reddit—and arguably every other single media site on the internet. People can still search for Reddit discussions, but Google's results increasingly allow them to consume information from those discussions without visiting Reddit itself. Search referrals also bring back existing users, meaning fewer clicks can affect both new-user acquisition and the platform's ability to keep people engaged.

Reddit, the erstwhile front page of the internet, is now pushing users to subscribe so it can better target them with ads.

CEO Steve Huffman on Thursday posted on Reddit that for users to get the "best" of Reddit, it will require personalization. "We'd also like more of our users to benefit from the core functionality and value of Reddit, which requires being logged in."

To be clear, Huffman said logging in doesn't mean you'll need to share your name or identity, which he says the site's ad business doesn't need.

Still, once reliant on search traffic, the forum website and last bastion of the open internet is rotating to ads. You know how if you wanted real people rather than ads to answer your questions, you'd add 'reddit' to whatever your search query was? It's going to get a lot harder to do that. And, of course, the market hates it.

One stock. Nvidia-level potential. 30M+ investors trust Moby to find it first. Get the pick. Tap here.

Reddit stock fell over 30% as of Friday afternoon, the worst single day for the stock since it has been a public company.

The reason wasn't the quarterly results, where Reddit posted a narrow beat on both EPS and revenue, though it slashed fourth-quarter guidance to $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below Wall Street's $1.05 billion expectation. It's because Reddit built its core business on referrals from Google Search over the last few years, and those referrals have sharply declined. Hence, the walled garden, subscription, ad-supported pivot.

But it's also something of a bellwether for the broader shift from an open internet, to a closed and logged-in one. That's driven by the rise in AI, where instead of searching for webpages, people get their answers directly from chatbots.

Reddit stock is down 62% since January 1. The company that emerges from the slide may be nearly unrecognizable to the forum's power users who fell in love with it well over a decade ago.

title: Reddit's Q3 User Miss Led by Soft Search-Referral Traffic, BofA Says
detail:
PREMIUM
Reddit's Q3 User Miss Led by Soft Search-Referral Traffic, BofA Says
MT Newswires
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 10:59 AM EDT 1 min read
RDDT
BAC
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit's (RDDT) Q3 user miss was driven by weaker search-referral traffic, which declined further in October, with current trends pointing to a low-double-digit decline in daily active users in Q4, BofA Securities said Friday in a note.

Reddit's Q3 revenue was $895 million, exceeding Street estimates. Q3 daily active users were 130.3 million, below the Street consensus, driven by a decline in Google search referral traffic, according to the note.

The company is shifting marketing spend toward app installs and plans to test a logged-in-only experience internationally in Q4, BofA noted. The firm expects the transition to a logged-in user experience to take multiple quarters and weigh on headline traffic trends, the note added.

However, the change could result in a higher quality user base, improve monetization and eliminate the Google traffic overhang, the brokerage said. BofA expects sentiment to remain subdued for a few quarters until Reddit demonstrates positive growth momentum for US logged-in users.

BofA kept a neutral rating on Reddit and lowered its price target to $135 from $190.

Shares of Reddit were down 26% in Friday trading.

title: Reddit shares plunge 26% despite earnings beat as user growth and outlook disappoint
detail:
Reddit shares plunge 26% despite earnings beat as user growth and outlook disappoint

RDDT

Reddit Inc (NYSE:RDDT) (NYSE: RDDT) shares plunged 26.07% to $95.82 in early trading on Friday, despite the social media company beating third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, as investors reacted to weaker fourth-quarter guidance and slowing user growth.

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $895 million, up 53% from a year earlier, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $886.34 million.

Diluted earnings per share were $1.40, up from $0.80 a year earlier and beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.31.

Advertising revenue, which accounts for most of the business, rose 54% to $847 million, while other revenue increased 35% to $48 million.

Net income climbed 74% to $283 million, while adjusted EBITDA, a measure of operating profitability, rose 70% to $402 million.

However, daily active unique users increased 12% to 130.3 million, below analysts' expectations of 134 million, while weekly active unique users rose 16% to 515.2 million.

Chief executive Steve Huffman warned that declining referrals from Google search had accelerated towards the end of the third quarter, and said daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter if the trend continued.

The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below the analyst estimate of $1.046 billion, while adjusted EBITDA is expected to range from $480 million to $510 million.

Reddit said it would test a logged-in-only experience outside the US later this year, seeking to prioritise more engaged users as changes to search reduce traffic from people who browse without signing in.

The company generated $364 million in operating cash flow and $363 million in free cash flow during the quarter, while holding $3.03 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.

Reddit repurchased about 670,000 shares for $100 million during the quarter, at an average price of $149.81.
